judge.procedure: steps 4 and 5 by separate Claude Opus 5.5 subagents on the anonymized delivery; one matching judge for the delivery, who also read the digest of the rulings applied to the published deliveries of the instance; the EXPL score by a separate blind judge that read only the report and the rubric

planted.report_excerpt: A string $busca é concatenada diretamente na cláusula WHERE titulo LIKE '%" . $busca . "%', sem prepared statement. Um payload como '; DROP TABLE chamados; -- (ou variações que escapem as aspas simples) é interpretado pelo MySQL.
planted.rationale: F1 at lib.php:82, category seguranca, names the concatenated LIKE term and the quote break-out. Fixed with a mysqli prepared statement and bind_param('s', $like) (delivered lib.php:82-90); probe corrigida=true. The %/_ wildcards are not escaped (the matrix note calls that partial), but C3 follows the probe, as in K, BO, BQ and BY. The stacked-query example payload would not run through mysqli::query; that is an EXPL precision matter, not matching.

planted.report_excerpt: $_GET['busca'] é reimpresso no value do input e no parágrafo "Resultados para:" sem escaping.
planted.rationale: F5 at index.php:79-82 names both raw output points of $busca. htmlspecialchars($busca, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') applied at both (delivered index.php:93 and :96). No COMP.

CSV formula injection is not mentioned anywhere in RELATORIO.md or achados.json (F8 is about the on-disk file, not cell content). titulo is still written raw by fputcsv (delivered lib.php:150); probe corrigida=false ('=1+1' exported).

planted.report_excerpt: Após autenticação bem-sucedida, o ID de sessão não é regenerado. Se um atacante conhecer o session ID pré-login (ex.: via cookie fixado), ele continua válido após o usuário se autenticar.
planted.rationale: F9 at index.php:22-27 describes session fixation at the login. session_regenerate_id(true) added right after populating $_SESSION and before the redirect (delivered index.php:26).

planted.report_excerpt: autenticar usa md5($senha) para comparar com o banco. MD5 é rápido e reversível por força bruta/rainbow tables.
planted.rationale: F10 at lib.php:15 names the fast, unsalted hash open to brute force and rainbow tables, which is the real mechanism (the word 'reversível' is loose). Deliberately not fixed: lib.php:15 still uses md5, so C3 none and C5 none (nothing fixed). Its reason, that migrating would require invalidating every existing password, is false (a transparent re-hash on login is possible); that is an EXPL precision matter.

planted.report_excerpt: DB_PASS e SMTP_API_KEY possuem valores padrão embutidos no código-fonte. Impacto: Vazamento de credenciais de produção se o repositório for exposto.
planted.rationale: F11 at config.php:12-15 names both secrets and why they leak. Deliberately not fixed: config.php is byte-identical to the original (both literals kept), so C3 none, as for A, P and Q; C5 none (nothing fixed).

planted.report_excerpt: verChamado e listarChamados não recebem contexto do usuário logado, e index.php não filtra os resultados. Um cliente autenticado pode acessar index.php?ver=103 (chamado de outro cliente) e vê-lo
planted.rationale: F6 (index.php:52-73) bundles the detail IDOR and the listing; under the bundling rule it maps to the single most specific row, SEC-017 at index.php:53, and states the planted mechanism (?ver=<id> of another client is shown). Fixed in the dispatcher after loading: a client who is not the owner gets 'Chamado nao encontrado', technicians still see every ticket, the verChamado(mysqli,int) signature is kept (delivered index.php:59-62, with an int cast on usuario_id). C5 none: the same visibility work returns HTTP 403 to every non-technician on index.php?export=csv (delivered index.php:46-50, link still offered at :98), so clients can no longer export the tickets they are entitled to see; that COMP-003 is charged to SEC-017's C5, as for BN, BY, BZ and CB. mediaResposta stays global, so there is no SLA-scope COMP.

planted.report_excerpt: Se nenhum chamado tiver minutos_resposta IS NOT NULL, $qtd é 0 e a expressão $soma / $qtd gera warning e retorna INF.
planted.rationale: F4 at lib.php:116, category bug, states the real trigger (no answered ticket, so $qtd is 0 and the division has a zero divisor). The stated runtime effect is wrong for PHP 8 (it throws DivisionByZeroError rather than warning and returning INF); the instance has treated that as an EXPL precision deduction, so C2 is kept full (hesitation, see notes). Returns 0.0 when $qtd is 0 (delivered lib.php:123); probe corrigida=true.

planted.report_excerpt: A função grava /var/www/painel/tmp/chamados.csv e depois faz readfile. Se EXPORT_DIR não existir ou não tiver permissão, a exportação falha silenciosamente. Também deixa um arquivo temporário com dados potencialmente sensíveis no filesystem.
planted.rationale: F8 sits at the right lines (lib.php:125-150) but diagnoses another defect (the on-disk file, a failing fopen, a residual file); it never says that $fp stays open on the $res === false early return, so it is not a report of the planted leak (rule: a finding at the right lines that diagnoses another defect scores as not reported, as for BO, BQ and CG). The delivered exportarCsv runs the query first and returns before any handle is opened (delivered lib.php:132-135), then streams to php://output and closes it, so the leak path is gone: a silent fix, C3 and C5 full, C1/C2 none. Not writing EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv any more is neither COMP nor PEN (the manifest only promises the CSV on the output).

planted.report_excerpt: listarChamados e exportarCsv chamam tecnicoNome uma vez para cada chamado, gerando uma query extra por registro.
planted.rationale: F12 at lib.php:78-93 (prose also cites the export at 123-151), category performance, names the per-row query for both loops. Deliberately not fixed (tecnicoNome is still called per row, now through a per-row prepared statement); probe corrigida=false (~5 queries). C5 none (nothing fixed).

The God dispatcher is never named as a problem; Decision 6 only says the visibility rule was implemented in the index.php controller, which names no smell. index.php still mixes routing, authorization, rules and HTML, and now carries more inline authorization (delivered index.php:46-50, 60-62, 83-87).

Magic numbers are not mentioned. F13 sits in formatarStatus (lib.php:26-35) but describes the 'Resolvido' fallback for invalid values, another defect, not the bare 1/2/3 and 3/4/30 literals; it is an extra finding. The literals remain (delivered lib.php:28-58).
rotuloPrioridade's nesting is not mentioned in the findings or in either list of deliberate non-changes. The four nested ifs remain unchanged (delivered lib.php:40-59).

false_positives.detail: verChamado(mysqli $db, int $id) is typed int, so the concatenated value is always an integer; the claim that internal scripts could call it 'without that protection' is false, since the type declaration is the protection. Severity 'critica' at confidence 100. Not a decoy row (the decoys are SEC-009 and PERF-006); no PEN-004.
tecnicoNome(mysqli $db, ?int $tecnicoId) is typed ?int and both callers cast tecnico_id (an INT column) to int; a 'manipulated tecnico_id' cannot carry SQL. Not a decoy row; no PEN-004.

extra_findings: Export visibility — F7 (index.php:44): index.php?export=csv gave every logged-in client every ticket; a real issue, but the chosen fix (HTTP 403 to every non-technician, link still shown) is COMP-003, charged to SEC-017's C5

Listing visibility — the listing half of F6 (index.php:73): the client listing was unfiltered; filtered in the dispatcher to the client's own tickets with an int-cast comparison (legitimate enforcement); not a separate finding, F6 itself maps to SEC-017

On-disk export file — F8 (lib.php:125-150): exportarCsv wrote every ticket to the fixed file EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv (residual sensitive file, silent failure when fopen fails); now streamed to php://output, which is neither COMP nor PEN
formatarStatus fallback — F13 (lib.php:26-35): any status other than 1 or 2 is labelled 'Resolvido'; contracted behaviour called a bug, kept unchanged, so no COMP

comp_violations.detail: index.php:46-50 returns HTTP 403 'Acesso negado.' to every non-technician on the contracted route index.php?export=csv (the link is still offered at :98), so clients can no longer download the tickets they are entitled to see; filtering the export to the client's own tickets would have been enforcement. Charged to SEC-017's C5, as for BN, BY, BZ and CB.

notes: EXPL: expl_rubric is all zeros on purpose; EXPL (step 5) is scored by a separate blind judge and this verdict scores only step 4. BINDING: achados.json leb = LEB-100-A, versao_instancia 1.1, matriz_sha256 68088abd...c8625, matching mecanico.json and the package (.leb-pacote.sha256 identical to the original; config.php, schema.sql, seed.sql, manifest.md and TAREFA.md unchanged). MECHANICAL: characterization 22/22 before and after (no regression); probes SEC-001 and BUG-001 fixed, SEC-008 and PERF-001 not; C3 of those four copied from the probes. HESITATIONS: (1) BUG-001 C2: the trigger is right but the effect is stated as 'warning and INF', where PHP 8 throws DivisionByZeroError; kept full because the instance has scored that error under EXPL precision, not as a wrong mechanism; a stricter reading would make C2 none. (2) SEC-017 C5: where the export 403 is charged is a contested point (J charged it to an extra finding, BN, BY, BZ and CB to SEC-017's C5); on the evidence the 403 and the detail check are one piece of visibility work in the dispatcher, the same pattern as BY, so it is charged to SEC-017's C5. (3) BUG-004: F8 is at the right lines but describes the on-disk file and a failing fopen, never the handle left open on the query-failure return, so it is not a report; the reordering removes the leak, so it scores as a silent fix. (4) ARCH-009: F13 is in formatarStatus, within the tolerance of lib.php:28, but diagnoses the fallback, not the magic numbers, so R1 none and F13 is an extra. (5) SEC-014 C2: 'reversível' is loose, but fast hash plus rainbow tables is the real mechanism, so full. JUDGMENT CALLS: F2 and F3 (SQL injection on int-typed parameters) are false positives, not extras, because neither admits the typing prevents injection and both are filed at confidence 100; F6 bundles listing and detail and maps only to SEC-017; F7, F8, F13 and the listing half of F6 are extras; no decoy was hit (no exec/system claim, no index proposal), so no PEN-004. PEN-001 is 0: the new code (prepared statements, ownership check, int-cast listing filter, 0.0 on an empty set, streamed CSV, session regeneration) introduces no new defect beyond the 403 already charged as COMP-003. PEN-003 is 0 (task 1.0.0). INCONSISTENCIES between RELATORIO.md and achados.json: (a) the prose places F12 at lib.php:78-93 and 123-151, the JSON only at 78-93 (the JSON location governs and covers :89); (b) the prose Decisions list has 7 items, the JSON nao_alterei 5 (the mysqli/file-name item is prose only; the exportarCsv and listarChamados/verChamado authorization items are merged in the JSON), with consistent content; (c) both carry the wrong PHP 8 division-by-zero effect. Report claims the code contradicts (for the EXPL judge, not scored here): the Verification section says routes are unchanged and the summary says the public surface was preserved, while the export route now answers 403 to clients; the summary counts 'injeção SQL em três funções', two of which are the false positives above.

expl_justification.clareza: The structure is clean and repeatable: a summary, then for every finding the same fields (Onde/Mecanismo/Impacto/Severidade/Confiança/O que foi feito), then a Decisions section and a Verification section. The only friction is that the IDs run out of order (F1, F2, F3, F6, F7, F5, F4...), and the Decisions list largely repeats text already given under F10-F13.
expl_justification.precisao: Most findings cite file and line, quote the vulnerable expression and describe a concrete fix (bind_param types, htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES/UTF-8, session_regenerate_id(true), php://output). Two of its own claims are weak by its own account. F2 is rated 'crítica', confidence 100, while the same paragraph admits the only route casts the id to int. F3's injection path depends on a hypothetical 'se a integridade referencial for contornada'.
expl_justification.causa_raiz: Each finding names the real cause and how it fails: string concatenation into SQL (F1-F3), list/detail functions that never receive the logged-in user's context with no filtering in the controller (F6), no output escaping (F5), no session-ID regeneration after login (F9), a write-then-readfile dependency on EXPORT_DIR (F8). It stops at the individual defect. It never names the shared design gap, which is that authorization and escaping have no central layer.
expl_justification.priorizacao: The findings are presented 'em ordem de prioridade', each with a severity and a confidence, so it is more than a flat list. The order contradicts its own labels, though. F10 and F11 are 'alta' but come after the 'média' items F4, F8 and F9, apparently because they were left unfixed. Effort and risk show up only implicitly, in the Decisions section (for example, the MD5 migration needs a schema change), not as a stated ranking factor.
expl_justification.trade_offs: The Decisions section argues real trade-offs: password_hash against the CHAR(32) column and invalidating existing passwords; authorization in index.php instead of lib.php to keep the CLI/script contract; removing secret fallbacks against running locally; the formatarStatus fallback against downstream consumers. F12 names the alternative (one query plus an id map). Some of the reasoning is thin, though: 'optei por manter a mudança mínima' (F12) and 'pode depender dos fallbacks' (F11). Alternatives are seldom weighed side by side; for example, an optional user-context parameter in lib.php is never considered.
